claims.text: Tailored thermomechanical processing can induce an ultrafine duplex lamellar microstructure in eutectic high-entropy alloys.
The processed ultrafine lamellar structure improves strength relative to the as-cast or minimally processed condition.
The processed ultrafine lamellar structure improves ductility while retaining high strength.
The processed ultrafine lamellar structure increases Young's modulus.
The processed ultrafine lamellar structure improves fracture resistance.
The starting cast AlCoCrFeNi-based eutectic alloy has a coarse as-cast microstructure.
The starting eutectic alloy contains alternating soft and hard phases.
A specific sequence of hot rolling, cold rolling, and rapid annealing refines the microstructure while retaining its lamellar phase distribution.
Optimized processing temperatures and deformation rates are required to avoid grain coarsening and embrittlement.
The processing strategy is applicable specifically to HEAs with eutectic or multiphase tendencies.
The refined duplex structure produces a microcrack-arresting mechanism.
Hard phases contribute increased strength.
Hard phases raise Young's modulus.
Soft phases accommodate plastic deformation and thereby contribute ductility.
Microstructural refinement increases dislocation accumulation and dynamic recovery through interphase load sharing.
A two-hierarchical constraint effect contributes to the improved mechanical response.
Tensile strength will improve by approximately 10–20% relative to the state of the art.
Fracture toughness will improve by approximately 10–20% relative to the state of the art.
The strategy may be ineffective in single-phase HEAs or alloys lacking clear phase separation.
Excessive deformation or over-annealing can destabilize the lamellar structure and negate the mechanical benefits.

contradictions.description: The main hypothesis requires simultaneous improvement in all four properties, but the falsification rule treats improvement in only three of the four as sufficient to avoid falsification.

The predicted gains are stated relative to the state of the art, whereas the operational baseline and experiment compare against an as-cast or standard-processed condition; these are not necessarily the same comparator.

The proposed initial state is described as coarse and as-cast, but the cited exemplar used as baseline evidence, AlCoCrFeNi2.1, is explicitly reported to possess a fine as-cast lamellar microstructure.
